summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for shortness of breath, left-sided chest pain, and bilateral foot swelling. She had increased use of albuterol and nebulizers at home, with a cough producing yellow sputum and subjective chills. Evaluation revealed no acute cardiopulmonary process on chest X-ray, normal troponin, and stable labs. Her symptoms were attributed to an acute asthma exacerbation, possibly triggered by a mild respiratory infection. She was treated with a six-day prednisone taper, a five-day course of azithromycin, and continued bronchodilator therapy. Her chronic conditions, including hypertension, rheumatoid arthritis, and chronic pain, were managed with baseline medications. She improved clinically, maintained oxygen saturation on room air, and was discharged home with instructions to complete her medications, continue home inhalers, and start a nicotine patch to aid smoking cessation. Follow-up was arranged with her primary care provider.
